data_provenance: synthetic crew data; vitamin storage losses from first-order kinetics anchored to published spaceflight-food retention data; physiology parameters from NASA/literature sources where available, otherwise assumed (see parameter_sources and /api/v1/health/parameters)

sources.citation: NASA JSC Nutritional Biochemistry Laboratory. Nutrition Requirements, Standards, and Operating Bands for Exploration Missions. Initial Release (rev 1), Dec 2005. NTRS 20200001703 (JSC-E-DAA-TN71711).
Cooper M, Perchonok M, Douglas GL. Initial assessment of the nutritional quality of the space food system over three years of ambient storage. npj Microgravity 3:17 (2017).

Goulette TR, Zhou J, Dixon WR, Normand MD, Peleg M, McClements DJ, Decker E, Xiao H. Kinetic parameters of thiamine degradation in NASA spaceflight foods determined by the endpoints method for long-term storage. Food Chemistry 302:125365 (2020; online 2019).
sources.access: abstract only (Europe PMC); full text paywalled, kinetic parameters (rate constants, temperature sensitivity) NOT accessed

sources.citation: Smith SM, Zwart SR, Block G, Rice BL, Davis-Street JE. The nutritional status of astronauts is altered after long-term space flight aboard the International Space Station. J Nutr 135(3):437-443 (2005).
sources.access: abstract only (Europe PMC); full text (Elsevier) returned HTTP 403

sources.citation: Rice BL, Zwart SR, Smith SM. Vitamin D in Real and Simulated Weightlessness: Implications for Earth. Conference abstract (ADA), NASA JSC. NTRS 20080026180. Reports the same n = 11 ISS cohort as SMITH_2005.

Modelling assumption of this project (no source).

scenario_preset.label: Small storage failure
scenario_preset.description: At Sol 150 the food-storage cooling fails for 45 Sols and peaks at 29.5 °C; the greenhouse goes offline. Vitamins in stored food break down faster. This is the default scenario.

status_rules.ACT: forecast Sols-to-risk <= 45 (vitamin C, B1 pools or vitamin D status)
status_rules.WATCH: forecast Sols-to-risk <= 120 or |z| of any vital >= 2.0 (vs a trend-following personal reference lagged 28 Sols)
status_rules.driver: largest contributor relative to its rule threshold: 120 / Sols-to-risk (nutrient forecast) vs |z| / 2.0 (vital); ACT is always forecast-driven
status_rules.CALIBRATING: personal baseline + trend window not yet available

vitamin_d_meta.label: Vitamin D (25-OH-D)
vitamin_d_meta.model: 25-OH-D declines exponentially (no UV in flight); rate scales with intake shortfall vs 25 ug/day
